whatItIs.heading: What makes sewage clean-up different from ordinary water damage?
whatItIs.body: The IICRC S500 standard classifies water intrusion into three categories based on contamination level. Category 1 is clean water—a supply-line break or appliance overflow. Category 2 is gray water—significant contamination but not sewage. Category 3 is black water—sewage backup, toilet overflow, sewer line failure, or septic system breach. Black water contains human waste, bacteria, viruses, parasites, and in some cases hydrogen sulfide and methane gas. Any porous material it contacts—carpet, drywall, insulation, wood subflooring—must be removed, not dried. The area must be treated with commercial-grade antimicrobial agents, and air quality must be verified before occupancy resumes. No amount of consumer-grade cleaning achieves a safe, documented result in a Category 3 event. The health exposure risk for untrained occupants attempting DIY remediation is real: direct contact, inhalation of aerosolized contaminants, and gas accumulation are all documented hazards.

steps.title: Rapid response and hazard assessment
steps.body: A real person answers at any hour. The crew arrives within 60 minutes wearing full PPE and immediately assesses the contamination boundary, identifies safety hazards—gas accumulation, electrical exposure in wet areas—and establishes containment before any other work begins.

steps.title: Extraction, containment, and affected-material removal
steps.body: Standing sewage is extracted with dedicated equipment kept separate from clean-water gear. All porous materials in the contamination zone—carpet, pad, drywall, insulation—are removed and bagged for disposal per health and safety regulations. Non-porous surfaces are cleaned and prepared for disinfection.

steps.title: Antimicrobial treatment and air scrubbing
steps.body: Commercial-grade antimicrobial agents are applied to all affected structural surfaces. HEPA air scrubbers run throughout this phase to capture aerosolized contaminants. Odor neutralization equipment addresses gases embedded in structural materials. Treatment continues until environmental testing confirms clearance.

steps.title: Structural drying, reconstruction, and documentation
steps.body: Once the area clears contamination testing, structural drying proceeds as on any water-damage job. Gallagher then transitions into reconstruction—replacing removed drywall, flooring, and trim—under the same project management. Full documentation supports the insurance claim from day one.

signs.heading: Situations that require professional sewage clean-up immediately
signs.intro: Sewage contamination does not resolve on its own. Every hour of delay expands the contamination boundary.

items.title: Sewage backup through floor drains or toilets
items.body: Raw sewage entering the home through any drain is a Category 3 event. Evacuate the affected area and call immediately—do not attempt extraction without full PPE and a plan for proper waste disposal.

items.title: Toilet overflow beyond the immediate bowl area
items.body: A toilet overflow that reached the floor and spread beyond the bathroom has contaminated the flooring, subfloor, and potentially the wall base. The contamination boundary is almost always larger than it appears.

items.title: Septic system failure or backup
items.body: A failing or overloaded septic system that pushes waste toward or into the home is a Category 3 event regardless of volume. Septic waste carries the same pathogen load as municipal sewer backup.

items.title: Sewer gas odor inside the home
items.body: Hydrogen sulfide and methane from sewer lines are toxic and potentially explosive at certain concentrations. A persistent sewage odor without visible backup warrants immediate inspection of drain traps, vent lines, and the surrounding slab.

items.title: Any flooding where the water source is unknown
items.body: Floodwater that entered from outside or from a source that could have contacted the sewer system is treated as Category 3 until proven otherwise. Downgrading contamination category without testing creates health and liability exposure.

whyUs.heading: Why Southern California homeowners call Gallagher for sewage clean-up
whyUs.body: Sewage clean-up is one of the most health-critical restoration categories, and it is also one of the most frequently mishandled by contractors who treat it like ordinary water damage. Gallagher Restoration Co. has handled Category 3 events across Southern California for more than 15 years—sewer backups in aging residential lines, septic failures in rural Riverside County, toilet overflows that migrated into wall cavities and subfloors before the homeowner realized the scope. The crew arrives in full PPE, establishes containment before touching the contaminated area, removes all porous materials that cannot be disinfected, applies commercial-grade antimicrobials, and documents every phase for the insurance file. IICRC-trained technicians classify contamination category correctly—a step that directly affects what your insurance carrier covers. One crew handles the job from extraction through reconstruction. Call (951) 541-0034 any hour.

pricing.heading: Sewage clean-up pricing—what to expect
pricing.body: Sewage clean-up costs are driven by the area affected, the materials that must be removed, and the extent of structural drying and reconstruction required afterward. Most residential sewage events handled by Gallagher Restoration Co. fall in the $1,500–$12,000 range. A contained toilet overflow in a single bathroom with limited porous material contact sits toward the lower end. A sewer backup that pushed into multiple rooms, reached wall cavities and subfloor across a large area, and requires significant drywall and flooring removal sits toward the upper end or beyond. Every job starts with a free on-site assessment to define the contamination boundary and produce a written scope for your insurance carrier. Homeowners policies in California typically cover sudden sewer backup events; coverage depends on policy specifics and Gallagher coordinates directly with your adjuster.

faqs.q: Is sewage backup covered by homeowners insurance in California?
faqs.a: Many standard California homeowners policies include sewer backup coverage as an endorsement. Whether it is included depends on your specific policy. Gallagher Restoration Co. documents the event, contamination category, and affected scope from day one and coordinates directly with your adjuster. If coverage is disputed, thorough documentation is the most effective tool.

faqs.q: Why can't I clean up sewage backup myself?
faqs.a: Category 3 black water contains bacteria, viruses, parasites, and potentially toxic gases. Porous materials—carpet, drywall, insulation—that contact sewage must be removed, not dried and cleaned. DIY attempts without full PPE create direct exposure to pathogens and typically spread contamination further before the actual boundary is understood. Consumer-grade disinfectants do not achieve the penetration levels required on structural surfaces.

faqs.q: How long does sewage clean-up take?
faqs.a: Most residential sewage clean-up events—extraction, material removal, antimicrobial treatment, and structural drying—take three to seven days. Reconstruction of removed drywall, flooring, and trim adds time depending on scope. Gallagher documents the timeline throughout for the insurance claim.

faqs.q: Can I stay in my home during sewage clean-up?
faqs.a: In most Category 3 events, Gallagher recommends temporary relocation until extraction, material removal, and antimicrobial treatment are complete and air-quality readings confirm the space is safe. Exposure to aerosolized sewage contaminants is a genuine health risk, particularly for children and immunocompromised individuals.
